sonnet.problem: The question quotes the line from verse 4 and asks the baker to complete it with the missing word ("lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of who?"). That is guessing the next words of a line. Nothing Papa Dorin told earlier lets the baker reason out the answer, and the wrong answers (Family, Friends) are guesses of wording.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

sonnet.problem: The true/false card asks about "a form of godliness" before any story card has told verse 5. Card 4 ends at verse 4, so the baker can only guess. Card 7 then tells the same fact after the question has already been asked.
sonnet.rule: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

sonnet.problem: No story card tells verse 9 (they will not advance much further) before this true/false card asks about it, and the same goes for card 16. The baker has no setup to reason from, so the pick comes down to luck.
sonnet.rule: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
